title: In-flight Telemetry Gatekeeper: SDK Adapter for Context-preserving Low-overhead Sampling
creator: Maya Singh
description: Introduce an SDK-side "gatekeeper" adapter that enforces deterministic, low-overhead sampling and metadata gating for in-flight requests across Redwood SDKs. Goal is to provide a consistent sampling decision and compact provenance envelope that travels with in-progress requests, minimizes header/key-value bloat, and lets downstream services reconstruct trace lineage with minimal CPU/io. This ticket covers implementation for Node and Python SDKs, integration tests, canary rollout plan, and performance validation against our 99th-percentile latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: SDK adapters for Node and Python emit a single compact telemetry envelope header (max 256 bytes) under 'x-rw-telemetry' when sampling decision applies
Sampling decision deterministic across retries and forked async paths (reconstruction should not create duplicate sampled traces)
Average added latency for a sampled request < 0.25ms (p50) and p99 < 2ms on current SDK baseline
Gatekeeper supports dynamic sampling rate overrides from Console (via runtime config) and falls back to local policy if control plane unavailable
Integration tests that emulate concurrent fork+retry scenarios pass and show stable trace IDs and canonical parentage
Documentation page in Dev Docs with migration notes and header decoding examples
technical_notes: Use compact binary protobuf-lite for the telemetry envelope with optional TLV fields to allow forward-compatibility; the envelope is base64url-encoded for safe header transport
Sampling RNG seeded from request-derived stable fingerprint (client id + timestamp-windowed salt) to ensure deterministic sampling across retries and short-lived retry loops
Offer an opt-in 'full-headers' mode for customers who need verbose baggage during rollout; default is 'compact'
Provide a context bridge that rehydrates envelope into existing OpenTelemetry span attributes for downstream SDKs that can't parse the binary header directly
Implement a lightweight C-extension for Python path bytes handling to avoid GC churn in hot paths; Node uses Buffer pooling
Fallback behavior: on malformed or oversized envelope, SDK will drop envelope and continue without sampling (emits local metric 'telemetry.gatekeeper.malformed')
Design doc: links to schema, TLV layout, and decoding pseudocode are in Confluence (see links)
